entities.summary:
ESCP Business School, established on December 1, 1819, in the 11th arrondissement of Paris, France, is one of the world's oldest business schools and is recognized for its pioneering role in business education. It was founded by a group of entrepreneurs and educators led by the visionary Henri de Villeneuve-Bargemont, who sought to create an institution that would meet the growing demand for formal business training in the wake of the Industrial Revolution. Over the years, ESCP has expanded its reach across Europe, with campuses in London, Berlin, Madrid, Turin, and Warsaw, thus making its influence felt in the broader context of international business education.

Throughout its history, ESCP has made significant contributions to the development of business curricula and practices. The school introduced innovative teaching methods and a unique pedagogy that combined theoretical knowledge with practical application, which became a model for other institutions. By the late 19th century, ESCP developed a strong reputation, leading to a network of alumni who would go on to impact various sectors, from finance to technology. In 1973, it became the first business school to establish an international curriculum, further solidifying its role as a leader in global business education.

The legacy of ESCP Business School extends beyond its immediate contributions to education; it has played a crucial role in shaping the landscape of European business practices and management education. Alumni include influential leaders such as Louis Gallois, former CEO of Airbus Group, and Michel Bon, former CEO of France Télécom, who have carried forward the school's ethos into their respective fields. The school has also been instrumental in fostering a pan-European identity among business leaders and continues to adapt its programs to meet the needs of an ever-evolving global marketplace.
